W2·Tue · Why your sourdough is flat
Flat loaves happen to everyone. Lagom and I have had our share of pancakes since 2023. Five fixes that actually work — and if you'd rather skip the three-day project, we won't judge.

CAROUSEL — 7 slides, 1080x1920 (TikTok photo mode; crop 1080x1350 for Instagram). Footer on every slide: X of 7 · LAGOMBERRY.
Slide 1: HOOK: Why your sourdough is flat (it's probably #3)
Slide 2: 1. Your starter isn't at peak. Use it when it has doubled and domed — not before, not after it collapses.
Slide 3: 2. Wrong proof. Poke test: slow, partial spring-back = ready. Instant bounce = wait. No bounce = overproofed.
Slide 4: 3. No surface tension. Weak shaping is the #1 cause of pancake loaves. Drag the dough toward you until the skin is tight.
Slide 5: 4. Too much water for your flour. Drop hydration by 5% and try again.
Slide 6: 5. Oven not hot enough. Preheat the Dutch oven 45–60 min at 475–500°F, lid on for the first 20.
Slide 7: CTA: Or skip the 3-day project. Our starter Lagom does this every week. Pre-order a loaf — or take home a piece of Lagom and start your own. lagomberry.store

Slide 3: Day 1–2: cut side down on a wooden board. No bag.
Slide 4: Day 3–4: linen or paper bag. Plastic softens the crust and invites mold.
Slide 5: Longer: slice it, freeze it, toast straight from frozen.
Slide 6: Revive a tired loaf: splash of water on the crust, 5–8 min at 350°F.
